content_html:
Cusco is a magical destination, full of history, culture and impressive landscapes. If you are planning a solo trip to the capital of the ancient Inca Empire, prepare for an unforgettable experience. Traveling alone to Cusco can be an enriching adventure, but it also requires planning to make the most of your stay.

Why travel alone to Cusco?

Cusco is a perfect city for solo travelers due to its safety, the hospitality of its people and the variety of activities available. Whether you're looking for adventure, history, or a connection to nature, you'll find everything you need here.

Advantages of traveling alone to Cusco:
Total freedom: Organize your itinerary without depending on anyone.
Connection with other travelers: Cusco is a meeting point for backpackers and adventurers from all over the world.
Personal challenge: Altitude and hiking require effort, which will allow you to overcome challenges and gain self-confidence.

Tips for traveling alone to Cusco

1. Acclimatization and health

Cusco is 3,399 meters above sea level, so altitude sickness (soroche) can affect you in the first days. To avoid it:

  • Rest and avoid physical exertion on your first day.
  • Drink coca tea or chew coca leaves.
  • Stay hydrated and avoid heavy meals.

2. Where to stay

If you travel alone, hostels are an excellent option to meet people. Some popular options are:

  • wild rover (party and social).
  • Pariwana (balanced atmosphere between party and rest).
  • Ecopackers (quieter and more comfortable).

If you prefer something more private, there are hotels and Airbnbs with great views of the historic center.

3. How to get around the city

  • On foot: Cusco is a walkable city, but be prepared for steep, cobblestone streets.
  • Taxis and public transport: Only use authorized taxis or apps like InDriver.
  • Organized tours: They are a safe and comfortable option for excursions to Machu Picchu, the Sacred Valley and the Mountain of 7 Colors.

Unmissable experiences for a solo traveler

1. Explore the Historic Center

Walk through the Plaza de Armas, visit the Cusco Cathedral and explore the bohemian neighborhood of Saint Blaise, full of cafes and art galleries.

2. Machu Picchu: Tour or on your own?

If you travel alone, you can choose between:
Organized tour: Includes transportation, tickets and guide, ideal to avoid complications.
On your own: Travel by train or the alternative route through Hidroeléctrica if you are looking for adventure and savings.

3. Unforgettable excursions

  • Mountain of 7 Colors and Red Valley: A demanding hike but with spectacular views.
  • Humantay Lagoon: Perfect for nature and hiking lovers.
  • Sacred Valley of the Incas: Pisaq, Ollantaytambo and Moray are mandatory stops.

4. Try local cuisine

Enjoy typical dishes such as:
Lomo saltado – Sauteed meat with potatoes and rice.
Cusco pork rinds – Fried pork with nickname.
Quinoa and Andean soups – Healthy and comforting options.

For cheap food, try local markets like Saint Peter. If you are looking for something more gourmet, restaurants like Chicha by Gastón Acurio or Pachapapa They are excellent options.

5. Nightlife and socializing

Cusco has a vibrant nightlife with bars and clubs like Mama Africa, Ukukus and Mythology. In addition, hostels often organize activities for socializing.

Let nothing stop your trip, the true experiences are what many do not dare to do.
